change_summary: Replay-only SEC 13F same-manager co-accumulation peer graph as peer-shock laggard admission source.
changed_variable: Use SEC 13F shared-manager co-accumulation edges as the peer-adjacency source for peer-shock laggard admission.
hypothesis: candidate_pool: SEC 13F co-accumulation peer graph, where the same institutional managers increased both names across consecutive filing windows, may admit cleaner peer-shock laggards than static co-ownership and beat rolling-correlation peer-shock after costs.

post_run_reflection.forbidden_near_neighbor_retry: Do not retry by sweeping min_accumulation_increase_pct, min_shared_accumulating_managers, min_coaccumulation_lift, manager holding-count bounds, top-K, hold days, cooldown, or notional on these frozen windows.
post_run_reflection.new_evidence_required: A valid retry needs non-quarterly ownership/flow evidence, active-manager conviction classification independent of holding count, manager-level alpha attribution, or closed forward replacement-value rows from a shared default-off helper.
post_run_reflection.why_result_happened: The same-manager co-accumulation graph did not clear the predeclared Gate-4 screen; 13F relation staleness and quarterly batch effects likely remain too noisy for peer-shock admission versus the accepted rolling-corr relation.

prediction.confidence_reason: exp-20260622-006 rejected static co-ownership but explicitly left holdings-change co-movement as a valid new evidence axis; co-accumulation should be less index-overlap-heavy than static co-hold, though quarterly filing lag and sample size are major risks.
